sources.claim: An EIN can be obtained directly from the IRS for free ("you never have to pay a fee for an EIN"); if forming an LLC, partnership or corporation, form the entity with the state first or the EIN application may be delayed.

The online application names a "responsible party" (an individual who controls the business) with an SSN or ITIN, is for businesses located in the US or its territories, and must be completed in one session.

sections.skill: Apply for an EIN through the official IRS source in the right order

questions.intro: The IRS lets businesses apply for an EIN directly, including online, at no charge. The online application asks for a "responsible party": an individual who controls the business, with a Social Security number (SSN) or ITIN. It is for businesses located in the US or its territories, and it must be completed in one session. The IRS advises forming an LLC, partnership or corporation with the state first; applying before the entity exists may delay things. Be careful with look-alike websites that charge fees.

sections.skill: The official counter versus a middleman

questions.prompt: In the story, who is the official counter?

choices.text: The stranger outside
The library desk
A bookstore
The parking lot

questions.correct_answer: The library desk
questions.intro: Imagine renewing a library card. You can go to the library desk and do it for free, or pay a stranger outside to stand in line for you. The stranger may help, but the library itself does not charge. Applying for an EIN is similar: the IRS is the official counter and does not charge. Websites that look official may add fees for doing the same thing.
